inventive_nucleus: An adjustable cavity design allows the built-in reference pressure sensor to be positioned at varying distances from the blood pressure cuff, compensating for potential calibration drift caused by changes in cuff material or wear over time.
mechanism: The adjustable cavity design interacts with the reference pressure sensor to detect changes in cuff material or wear over time.
causal_chain: s1: Idle period detection triggers the adjustable cavity design to adjust its position
s2: The reference pressure sensor detects changes in cuff material or wear over time
s3: The adjustable cavity design adjusts its position to compensate for calibration drift
s4: The reference pressure sensor analyzes sensor data to determine optimal calibration settings
s5: The microcontroller executes the calibration routine based on the reference pressure sensor's analysis
s6: The device provides accurate blood pressure readings with minimal calibration drift
system_architecture: Modular layout with the adjustable cavity design and reference pressure sensor in separate modules.
operating_conditions: The device operates in idle periods when not in use.
boundary_conditions: The adjustable cavity design contains the failure by allowing the reference pressure sensor to adjust its position and compensate for calibration drift.
expected_effect: The device provides accurate blood pressure readings with minimal calibration drift.
